titleZh: 第一次让计算机执行你的计算
title: Your first computer-executed calculation

blocks.text: This chapter begins with no programming knowledge. We distinguish files, programs, the Python interpreter, and a terminal before running a program of only a few lines. The mathematics uses arithmetic, parentheses, and units. The goal is not complex code, but a precise account of where the file is, which line executes, what each name stores, and how the result is checked.

blocks.caption: 第一次运行程序时要追踪的链条：从路径中的文件到终端中的证据。

blocks.text: You will create, run, and check a Python program in a new folder and diagnose one minimal error.
1.1 A computer does not understand the problem statement

blocks.right: 明确输入 + 明确步骤 + 可检查输出
blocks.note: 缺少任何一项，正确数字也可能来自错误程序。 / A plausible number can still come from the wrong program.

blocks.text: First make the scene explicit: an object moves from the 12 cm mark to the 19 cm mark. So 12 cm is the start, 19 cm is the finish, and the change is “finish minus start”: $19-12=7$ cm. A computer does not know this automatically. It processes values by explicit instruction and does not know that 19 is the finish, 12 is the start, or that the result is in centimetres. Programming therefore begins by turning omitted human knowledge into explicit steps.

blocks.title: 四个对象不要混淆 / Four objects not to confuse

items: 文件（file）：存储在磁盘上的内容，有名字和路径。
程序（program）：按照某种语言写成、准备让计算机执行的一组指令。
Python解释器（Python interpreter）：读取Python指令并执行它们的软件。
终端（terminal）：输入命令、启动程序和查看文字输出的界面。

blocks.text: Comparing a program file to an experiment procedure is imperfect but useful at first: the file stores steps, the interpreter executes them, and the terminal issues the command to execute this procedure now. Output produced during a run is not the program file itself.
1.2 File names, extensions, and paths

The file name `first_calculation.py` contains the stem `first_calculation` and the extension `.py`. The extension indicates Python source. A path locates the file in nested folders, for example `E:/codex/robotics-study/first_calculation.py`. Different folders can contain files with the same name, so saying “I ran `first_calculation.py`” is not yet precise.

blocks.title: Windows上的第一次准备 / First setup on Windows

blocks.text: Create a clearly named study folder such as `E:/codex/robotics-study`, then create `chapter01` inside it. The editor modifies files; PowerShell runs commands from a working directory. Before running a command, inspect the path shown in the terminal prompt.
1.3 The first program: predict each line
In the program below, `start_cm` stores the start (12 cm) and `finish_cm` stores the finish (19 cm). Therefore “finish minus start” is written as `finish_cm - start_cm` in code.

cells: 建立 `start_cm` 与数值12的关联
建立 `finish_cm` 与数值19的关联
计算终点减起点并保存

blocks.code:
start_cm = 12
finish_cm = 19
change_cm = finish_cm - start_cm

print(change_cm)

blocks.text: The first line associates the start, 12 cm, with `start_cm`; the second associates the finish, 19 cm, with `finish_cm`; the third evaluates finish minus start, `finish_cm - start_cm`, and associates the result with `change_cm`; the final line displays the result. Executed top to bottom, the output should be `7`.

blocks.title: 变量名不是数学未知数 / A variable name is not necessarily an unknown

blocks.text: After the third line executes, `change_cm` stores the definite value 7. A programming variable is usually a name associated with a value at the current moment; it is not necessarily an unknown such as $x$ in an equation. A name can later be associated with a new value, so execution order matters.
1.4 Saving and running the file

Save the code as `first_calculation.py`. In PowerShell, enter its folder and run `python first_calculation.py`. The first `python` starts the interpreter; the following file name tells it which program to read. If the terminal is not in the file's folder, change directory first or use the complete path.

The prompt, command, and output have different roles. The prompt shows the working directory; the command is your request; the following 7 is program output. Do not copy all terminal text into the Python file.
1.5 Values, names, operators, and expressions

The 12 and 19 are integer values. The minus sign is an operator. `finish_cm - start_cm` is an expression that produces a value when evaluated. Here the equals sign performs assignment: evaluate the right side, then associate the result with the name on the left. It does not assert that both sides are forever equal.

blocks.text: 1.6 Why units appear in names

Python does not prevent adding centimetres to metres. Including a unit in a simple name, such as `length_cm` or `speed_m_per_s`, is not a complete unit system, but it improves first reading and checking. Names use letters, digits, and underscores and cannot begin with a digit.

blocks.title: 厘米换成米 / Convert centimetres to metres

blocks.text: One metre equals one hundred centimetres, so 7 cm equals $7/100=0.07$ m. Predict the output before running the program below.
1.7 Does the program survive changed input?

One correct answer does not prove the rule. Change the start to 19 cm and finish to 12 cm; the prediction is -7. Then set both to 12 cm; the prediction is 0. These inputs check reverse motion and the boundary case of no motion.

blocks.title: 第一条程序检查原则 / The first program-checking rule

blocks.text: Use at least one ordinary case, one boundary case, and one reversed or substantially different case. A test is not designed to make the program pass; it is designed to expose an incorrect understanding of the rule early.
1.8 Reading an error for the first time

Deliberately change the last line to `print(change_mm)`. The program raises an error because the name `change_mm` was never created. An error is not a judgment of you; it is a record of where execution stopped. Read the final line first for the error type and nearby cause, then inspect the named file and line.

items: 预测：出错前哪些行能够执行？
定位：报错指出哪个文件、哪一行和哪一种错误？
比较：`change_mm` 与已经赋值的名字有什么不同？
修复：统一名称后重新运行，并确认输出是否恢复。

blocks.title: 不要一次修改许多地方 / Do not change many things at once

blocks.text: Changing the file name, directory, variable names, and formula together destroys causal information. Repair the nearest reported issue and run again. This identifies which change actually solved the problem.
1.9 Put a check inside the program
Python's `assert` expresses a condition that must hold here. If the condition is true, execution continues; if false, execution stops and reports the failed check.

blocks.code:
start_cm = 12
finish_cm = 19
change_cm = finish_cm - start_cm

assert change_cm == 7
print(change_cm)

blocks.text: The double equals `==` compares two values; the single equals `=` assigns. Deliberately change the expected value to 8 and observe execution stop before printing. An assertion does not prove correctness for every input, but it stores one concrete expectation in the program so later changes can be checked.
1.10 The first complete mini-experiment

Now compare three motion cases. We do not yet use loops or functions because those concepts have not been established. Repeating a few lines is inelegant, but it keeps every step visible. Later chapters show how to remove the repetition.

blocks.caption: 三个可检查的移动案例 / Three checkable motion cases
blocks.code:
"""First executable calculation for a reader with no programming background."""

start_1_cm = 12
finish_1_cm = 19
change_1_cm = finish_1_cm - start_1_cm
assert change_1_cm == 7

start_2_cm = 19
finish_2_cm = 12
change_2_cm = finish_2_cm - start_2_cm
assert change_2_cm == -7

start_3_cm = 12
finish_3_cm = 12
change_3_cm = finish_3_cm - start_3_cm
assert change_3_cm == 0

print(change_1_cm, change_2_cm, change_3_cm)

blocks.text: The predicted output is `7 -7 0`. The cases cover an ordinary case, a reversed case, and a boundary case. Text beginning with `#` is a comment: it explains code but is not executed as a Python instruction.
1.11 From ruler to robot without skipping levels

The position of a mobile robot on a line, the angle of a robot joint, and the pixel location of a camera target can all begin with final value minus initial value. Their units and meanings differ. At this point, notice only the shared structure; vectors, matrices, and controllers are not yet required. Later chapters add multiple directions and time after one-dimensional change is clear.

blocks.text: 1.12 Exercises, answers, and completion standard

items: 建立 `chapter01` 文件夹和 `first_calculation.py`，运行并记录终端中的当前路径、命令和输出。
把起点和终点改为 $2.5$ m 与 $4.0$ m。先手算，再预测程序输出，然后运行。
故意把一个变量名拼错。记录错误类型、文件、行号和修复方法。
写三个断言，分别检查正向、反向和零变化。
解释为什么变量名中的单位不能阻止错误，但仍然比 `x` 和 `y` 更容易检查。
不运行代码，逐行说明1.10节中每个名字第一次获得值的时刻。

blocks.text: Exercise 2 gives $4.0-2.5=1.5$ m. Exercise 3 usually produces a `NameError`, but the actual final error line is authoritative. Exercise 4 must include positive, negative, and zero expectations. Exercise 5 should note that Python sees names and values but does not understand the unit embedded in a name; the benefit is human review. Exercise 6 must follow top-to-bottom execution rather than describe only the final result.

blocks.title: 本章完成证据 / Evidence of completion

blocks.text: You should independently create, save, and run a program in a new folder; distinguish prompt, command, and output; predict each line; repair one undefined name; and check three cases with assertions. If AI must still dictate every click or command, repeat Sections 1.2--1.4 and write the purpose of each step.
合上书，回答：程序文件、Python解释器、终端、命令和输出分别是什么？然后在一个新文件夹中重新完成一次正向、反向和零变化实验。
保存程序、终端命令、预期输出、实际输出和一次错误修复记录。下一章从数值、单位、变量和表达式继续，随后先学习列表、循环和条件，再进入代数、矩阵与 Jacobian，不会直接跳入 NumPy。
